q: Čech cohomology H̃ⁿ(X; G) agrees with singular cohomology for 'nice' spaces (CW-complexes). Its main advantage is that:
opts: It is defined for all topological spaces (not just CW-complexes) and is functorial and exact
It agrees with de Rham cohomology on manifolds
exp: Čech cohomology is defined for any topological space via good covers (or the nerve of covers). It agrees with singular and de Rham cohomology for manifolds/CW-complexes, but extends to more singular spaces where singular cohomology may misbehave.
